doc.title: Grover Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, February 13, 1996

title: Joe Williams and the Basie comeback
summary: Joe Williams was a huge factor in the band's 1950s resurgence and is a natural singer in any style.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Okay. Fair enough. My goodness. And Joe comes together with the band a few times a year, right?

You notice how natural it is when he does come in? Oh, no, no, no, Joe was a very, very big part of the comeback of this band. You know the big band business had really frittered down pretty well in the 50s, and Joe was a huge, huge factor in the resurgence of this band. I would be remiss to tell you differently. And the old man never forgot that and he was always very, you know, appreciative of the fact of how important Joe was to that stage of the career. And Joe is another genius-level vocalist. You can’t lose him, he’s, you know, I think he could do grand opera as well as what you see us doing here. A natural singer. Like Sarah Vaughan was the same way. I think Joe could do “Pagliacci” just as well as he can do the blues.
I almost heard that in the “Here’s To Life” tonight.
Oh, yeah, no, he’s a vocalist. Oh, he is a musician. And he has a great ear, you can’t lose him. He can sing the slowest tempo, and the fastest thing. You know he’s very —
